items.title: Have dbt skills been bitter lesson’d?
items.excerpt: Models have improved a lot since we shipped dbt agent skills, so I ran Claude Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku 5.5, and then Sonnet 4.5, through a Formula 1 dbt project with and without them. The 5.5 models already knew dbt, run-to-run noise was bigger than any skills effect, and what separated good runs from bad ones was process.

items.title: Managed warehouse for MLflow (Beta)
items.excerpt: With managed warehouse, users can view traces stored in Unity Catalog in the MLflow UI without selecting a SQL warehouse. MLflow runs trace queries on a SQL warehouse that it creates in your workspace when your workspace supports it, and on serverless compute otherwise. Workspace admins can enable Managed Warehouse for MLflow on the Previews page . See Managed warehouse for MLflow traces .

items.title: Claude Code auto mode for Anthropic and non-Anthropic models
items.excerpt: Claude Code auto mode is now supported for both Anthropic and non-Anthropic models hosted by Azure Databricks. Auto mode reviews tool calls to reduce routine permission prompts. See Auto mode .

items.title: Relationships between metric views (Beta)
items.excerpt: Relationships between Unity Catalog metric views are in Beta . Use ALTER VIEW ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... RELATIONSHIP to record how a source metric view joins to a target metric view, including the cardinality and the join condition, so that AI assistants and BI tools choose the right join path. Relationships require Databricks Runtime 19 and above, or a SQL warehouse. See Relationships between metric views .

items.title: Unpaginated requests to some Unity Catalog REST API operations will soon be rejected
items.excerpt: Azure Databricks will soon start rejecting unpaginated requests to some Unity Catalog REST API operations, such as list catalogs, list schemas, and list tables, with HTTP 400 responses. Prior to this, unpaginated requests to these operations are subject to progressively stricter rate limits and will receive HTTP 429 responses, potentially causing jobs to run more slowly due to retries, or fail if the client does not handle these errors. The paginated forms of these operations remain available. If you call these operations directly, update your clients to set max_results=0 and follow with next_page_token until all pages are retrieved. If you use a Databricks SDK or the Databricks CLI, upgrade to a current release, which uses these fields by default. For the full list of affected operations and update instructions, see Paginate Unity Catalog REST API operations .

items.title: dbt without the warehouse (or the bill): DuckDB end to end
items.excerpt: dbt v2 ships with a built-in DuckDB adapter, so connecting dbt to a local, offline warehouse takes only a small profile change.

items.title: Genie One enhancements
items.excerpt: Conversation outline : Use the conversation outline along the left edge of Genie One conversations to jump between your messages. Hover over a tick in the outline to preview a message and the start of its response. See Navigate a long conversation . Upload skills (Public Preview) : You can now click Upload skills to upload your existing skill files and folders to your skills folder in the workspace. See Upload a skill . Snippets from external tool queries (Public Preview) : Genie Ontology now also extracts snippets from queries that external tools , such as dbt, run on Azure Databricks. These runs appear in query history alongside queries that you run in Azure Databricks. See Genie Ontology . Remembered sign-in email in the Genie mobile app (Public Preview) : The Genie mobile app now remembers the email address of the last user who signed in and prefills it at the next sign-in. See Use Genie on mobile .

items.title: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview
items.excerpt: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview . You can cache a DataFrame with df.cache() or df.persist() on serverless compute to reuse an expensive result for the rest of your session. Caching requires serverless environment version 5 or above, Databricks Connect for Python 18.1.8 or above, or Databricks Connect for Scala 18.1.5 or above. The preview is enabled by default for most workspaces. Workspace admins can disable it from the Previews page. See Cache DataFrames on serverless compute .
